displayedInputs.question: The supplement of an angle measures \(120^\circ\). How many degrees is the complement of this angle?
If \(\angle\alpha=25^\circ18'\), its complement measures \(a^\circ b'\). Enter \(a\) and \(b\) in that order, separated by a comma.
The supplement of an angle is 3 times its complement. How many degrees is the angle?
If \(\angle 1+\angle 2=90^\circ\) and \(\angle 1+\angle 3=90^\circ\), what is the relationship between \(\angle 2\) and \(\angle 3\)? Why?

choices.A: \(\angle 2=\angle 3\), because supplements of the same angle are equal.
choices.C: \(\angle 2=\angle 3\), because complements of the same angle are equal.

displayedInputs.question: If \(\angle\alpha=\angle\beta\) and \(\angle\alpha=55^\circ\), how many degrees is the complement of \(\angle\beta\)?
\(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are supplementary, and \(\angle 3\) and \(\angle 2\) are supplementary. If \(\angle 1=40^\circ\), how many degrees is \(\angle 3\)?
Which of the following arguments is correct?

choices.A: Since \(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are supplementary, and \(\angle 2\) and \(\angle 3\) are supplementary, \(\angle 1=\angle 3\).
choices.D: Since \(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are complementary, \(\angle 3\) and \(\angle 4\) are supplementary, and \(\angle 2=\angle 4\), \(\angle 1=\angle 3\).

displayedInputs.question: Given \(\angle 1+\angle 2=180^\circ\), \(\angle 2+\angle 3=180^\circ\), \(\angle 1=2x+10^\circ\), and \(\angle 3=3x-20^\circ\), find the value of \(x\).

A track is 400 m per lap, and a straight section is 100 m long. What is the total length of the two bends? (One lap consists of two identical straight sections and two identical bends, with each straight section measuring 100 m; unit: m; enter only the numerical value.)
A student runs 3 and a half laps around a 400 m loop track. How many meters does the student run in total?

One lap along the inner edge of a track measures 400 m and consists of two identical straight sections (90 m each) and two semicircular bends. Use \(\pi=22/7\). The two semicircular bends together form a circle. What is the diameter of this circle in m?
In a 400 m race, the starting lines are at different positions in different lanes, with the starting lines for runners in the outer lanes farther forward. What is the main reason?

choices.A: Runners in the outer lanes have better physical fitness.
choices.B: The straight sections in the outer lanes are shorter.
choices.C: To make the competition venue more attractive.
choices.D: The bends in the outer lanes are longer, so their starting lines must be moved forward to ensure that runners in all lanes cover the same distance.

displayedInputs.question: A sketch of a venue uses a scale of \(1:1000\). A straight section measures 10 cm on the sketch. What is its actual length in m?
Two lines intersect. If one angle measures \(70^\circ\), what is the measure of an angle that forms a linear pair with it? (Unit: degrees; enter only the numerical value.)
Which of the following statements about linear pairs is correct?

choices.A: Angles in a linear pair are equal.
choices.B: Angles in a linear pair are supplementary.
choices.C: Angles in a linear pair are complementary.
choices.D: Two supplementary angles must form a linear pair.

displayedInputs.question: Two lines intersect, and one of the angles formed is 2 times an angle that forms a linear pair with it. How many degrees is this angle?
Among the four angles formed by two intersecting lines, how many linear pairs are there in total?
Two lines intersect. One angle is \(40^\circ\) greater than its adjacent supplementary angle. What is the measure of this angle in degrees?
Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at point \(O\). Which of the following pairs consists of vertical angles?
Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at point \(O\). Given \(\angle AOC=4x-15^\circ\) and \(\angle BOD=2x+35^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle AOC\) in degrees.
Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at point \(O\), and \(\angle AOC+\angle BOD=100^\circ\). What is the measure of \(\angle AOD\) in degrees?
In the same plane, how many lines through a point are perpendicular to a given line? (Enter a number.)
Which symbolic expression represents “line \(a\) is perpendicular to line \(b\)”?
Which is the correct method for using a set square to draw a perpendicular to line \(l\) through a point \(P\) outside \(l\)?

choices.A: Align one leg of the set square with \(l\), slide the set square along \(l\) until the other leg passes through point \(P\), and then draw a line along that leg.
choices.B: Align the hypotenuse of the set square with \(l\), and draw a line through point \(P\) in the direction of the hypotenuse.
choices.C: Draw any line through point \(P\), then use a protractor to measure that its angle with \(l\) is approximately \(90^\circ\).
choices.D: Place the vertex of an acute angle of the set square at point \(P\), then draw a line along the hypotenuse.

displayedInputs.question: In the same plane, \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are three distinct lines. If \(a\perp b\) and \(b\perp c\), what is the positional relationship between \(a\) and \(c\)?

choices.B: \(a\) and \(c\) intersect but are not perpendicular.

displayedInputs.question: Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at point \(O\), \(OE\perp AB\), and ray \(OE\) lies inside \(\angle AOD\). Given \(\angle AOC=50^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle COE\) in degrees.
The perpendicular segment from point \(P\) to line \(l\) has length \(3\) cm. Could the distance from \(P\) to another point \(Q\) on \(l\) be \(2\) cm?

choices.A: Yes, as long as \(Q\) is close enough to the foot of the perpendicular.
choices.B: No. The perpendicular segment is the shortest, so \(PQ\) is at least \(3\) cm.
choices.C: Yes, because \(PQ\) is not necessarily longer than the perpendicular segment.

displayedInputs.question: Point \(P\) lies outside line \(l\), and \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) are three points on \(l\). Given \(PA=5\) cm, \(PB=3\) cm, and \(PC=4\) cm, the distance from point \(P\) to line \(l\) is
How should the shortest canal from river \(l\) to village \(P\) be built?

choices.A: Build it in any direction; the length is the same.
choices.B: Build it in a direction parallel to \(l\).
choices.C: Draw a perpendicular to \(l\) through point \(P\) and build along the perpendicular segment, because the perpendicular segment is the shortest.
choices.D: Build it along the segment connecting \(P\) to any point on the riverbank.

displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(AC=3\) cm, \(BC=4\) cm, and \(AB=5\) cm. What is the distance from point \(C\) to line \(AB\), in cm? (Write your answer as a decimal.)
When two lines are cut by a third line, how many angles are formed in total?
When two lines are cut by a third line, how many pairs of corresponding angles are there in total?
Lines \(a\) and \(b\) are cut by line \(c\). Both \(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) lie between \(a\) and \(b\), and both are on the right side of \(c\). Then \(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are
When two lines are cut by a third line, how many pairs of corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, and same-side interior angles are there in total?
If \(a\parallel b\) and \(b\parallel c\), what is the positional relationship between \(a\) and \(c\)? (The lines lie in the same plane, and \(a\) and \(c\) do not coincide.)

choices.C: \(a\) and \(c\) intersect but are not perpendicular.

displayedInputs.question: Which symbolic expression represents “line \(a\) is parallel to line \(b\)”?
In the same plane, how many lines can be drawn through a point outside a given line that are parallel to the given line?
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: Through a point outside a given line, there is exactly one line parallel to the given line.
choices.B: Two lines that do not intersect are called parallel lines.
choices.C: Through a point, there is exactly one line parallel to a given line.
choices.D: Two lines parallel to the same line are perpendicular to each other.

displayedInputs.question: Three distinct lines \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) lie in the same plane, with \(a\parallel b\) and \(c\) intersecting \(a\). How many intersection points do these three lines have in total?
